paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see. The land was subdued, the fighting was over, and seven tribes were still sitting there with their inheritance unclaimed. Joshua asks them, "How long will you put off entering and possessing the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you?" (Joshua 18:3). A gift sitting in the box does you no good, and I know a few cookies that learned that the hard way.

Now look at how the land gets handed out. Men survey it, Joshua casts lots "in the presence of the LORD," and every tribe receives its share at Shiloh (Joshua 18:10). Nobody grabs, nobody argues over the biggest piece, and even Simeon's land sits inside Judah's because Judah's share was too large (Joshua 19:9). When the LORD hands out the portions, every tribe gets a place, and that's how it was done at Shiloh.

And here's the part I love. After every tribe has its land, the Israelites give Joshua his inheritance "as the LORD had commanded," and he gets the city he asked for, Timnath-serah (Joshua 19:50). He rebuilt it and settled in it. So, baker, whatever God has put in your hands, don't hit snooze on it. Step in, settle down, and get to work, because there's room in the Dorinverse for a baker who shows up.
